heading: Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier science.
lead: Different species have different physiology and transfusion requirements, but most vertebrates share hemoglobin-based oxygen transport.

foundation.title: From hemoglobin chemistry to effective oxygen delivery.
paragraphs: Hemoglobin binds oxygen through iron-containing heme groups. Oxygen delivery also depends on circulation, oxygen affinity, blood flow and tissue demand.

Hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers, or HBOCs, investigate a cell-free approach to oxygen transport. BHOC builds on this field as a Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier development platform. The objective is complementary oxygen-delivery support, not replacement of the wider functions of blood.

functionalDelivery.title: PCV is important. Functional oxygen delivery requires more.
paragraphs: Packed cell volume (PCV) measures the fraction of blood occupied by red cells. Cell-free plasma hemoglobin can add oxygen-carrying capacity without increasing red-cell volume, so PCV alone does not describe the whole oxygen-delivery system after an HBOC infusion.

Total hemoglobin, circulation, oxygen affinity and unloading, blood flow, tissue demand and clinical physiology all matter. P50 and the full oxygen dissociation curve also change with pH, carbon dioxide, temperature and the cell-free environment.

points.title: Measure the right compartment
points.text: PCV describes red-cell volume; it does not count plasma hemoglobin as red cells.

points.title: Connect carriage to delivery
points.text: Oxygen content, circulation, affinity, unloading and tissue extraction determine functional delivery together.

points.title: Keep evidence product-specific
points.text: Historical canine observations generate research questions; safety and tissue benefit require controlled product-specific evidence.

functionalDelivery.boundary: This interpretation comes from historical canine Oxyglobin material and general oxygen physiology. It is not a claim of BHOC efficacy or a reason to disregard PCV.

nature.title: Nature's bioengineering
nature.text: Most vertebrates use hemoglobin, with important exceptions such as Antarctic icefish. Conserved chemistry is a scientific starting point; species-specific physiology, dosing, safety and efficacy still require their own evidence.

chemistry.title: Heme and chlorophyll
chemistry.text: Both belong to related tetrapyrrole chemistry. Heme coordinates iron; chlorophyll coordinates magnesium. Their ring structures, side chains and biological roles differ. Hemoglobin transports oxygen; chlorophyll absorbs light in photosynthesis.
